text.p: - Alexander Lebed has launched an attack on Russia's budget, the paper writes in reference to the state security chief's tough criticism of the government's financial policy.
- Kazakhstan has destroyed its last silo suitable for the launch of the CC-18, the biggest Russian intercontinental ballistic missile.

- Natural concern about Boris Yeltsin's health seems to have developed into rude interference in the president's private life, the daily says about his political opponents' comments on the head of state.
- Boris Yeltsin on Thursday met a group of doctors, but has not yet made any decision about the transfer of his powers.

- General Vyacheslav Tikhomirov has suspended the withdrawal of Russian troops from Chechnya because of delays in the exchange of prisoners, but Lebed accused the commander of the federal forces in the region of being impulsive.

- Chechen separatists are increasing their political activity and maintaining their military presence in Grozny. Meanwhile, Moscow has protested against an invitation issued to rebel commander Aslan Maskhadov to Strasbourg to speak at a meeting of the Council of Europe.
- An Italian company has signed a deal worth $65 million with Russia's gas monopolist.
- Peace agreements reached between Lebed and Maskhadov are a purely political declaration, Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyev is quoted as saying.
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is not happy with many points of the Chechen peace accords but welcomes the main achievement -- a ceasefire, says the paper.

- Russia's armed forces are likely to fail to meet its demand for soldiers this year since 87 percent of young conscripts will be able to avoid army service for various reasons, the paper quotes a miliary recruitment official.
- One cannot rule out the possibility that President Yeltsin may decide to have his heart operation in the West, says the paper.
